answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before trading. One agent, one stake: spawning a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes, so sybil cost scales with size instead of being free. If an identity cheats, peers slash its stake and echo the verdict across the network, so the attacker loses money on every fake it burns. Honest agents treat the stake registry like an oasis of verified counterparts, and each identity carries a signed history, a sonnet of past deals that no fresh fake can forge for free.
